plain_english: Ninian was a fisher and burgess of Glasgow. His testament records his death in January 1613. The entry combines an inventory, debts, a latter will and subsequent court administration; the records before the opening on image 142 and after the upper continuation on image 145 belong to other people.

The latter will expressly calls Jonet Hutchesoun his spouse and Robert Glasgow his son. The next page separately names John Glasgow as his brother and Marioun Glasgow as his sister. Robert receives a stated legacy of one hundred pounds. A further bequest names Elizabeth Hutchesoun without stating her relationship.

The damaged lower part of image 143 and the continuation about maintaining someone cannot safely be used to make William another son. Nor does the spouse clause establish Jonet Hutchesoun as Robert's mother: that question belongs to the separate testament of Jonet Meik.
These are substantial family-clause readings, not a fully deciphered estate account. The financial parties, totals, exact clothing legacy and parts of the confirmation remain unresolved.
findings: Image 142, opening: occupation is fischer (fisher), not flesher; civic description is burgess of Glasgow.
Image 143, latter will: 'Jonet hutchesoun his spous' and 'Robert glasgow his sone' explicitly state the relationships, independently of executorship.
Image 144, opening legacies: John is expressly brother and Marioun expressly sister. Marioun must not be converted into a daughter.
Image 144: Robert is again called son, with an explicit 'ane hundreth pundis' bequest. Elizabeth Hutchesoun's receipt of a legacy does not establish kinship.
Neither the brother clause nor the shared surname securely identifies John with Glasgow-1030. The testament contains no fresh proof of Ninian's parents.
All four supplied pages were examined. This is full coverage of the supplied image span, but only a partial transcription of the surviving text.

Relationship assessment, 28 September 2026: combined with Ninian’s 1596 burgess admission as Robert Glasgow’s second son, the Marion sister clause, shared surname and compatible chronology support Robert as Marion’s confident inferred father. No concrete alternative father is known. This reassesses the existing records; no fresh manuscript wording is claimed. Marion’s mother remains uncertain.
